disposition_reason: Literature review and label survey with no original metal measurements; all concentrations are averages of values from other studies.

study.design: Conference proceedings paper: scoping literature review (11 studies, Web of Science 2018-2025) of metal(loid)s in pureed baby foods plus a labelling survey of fish-based purees in five Spanish supermarket chains
study.market: Spain (five main super/hypermarket chains, online and on-site near Vega Baja, Alicante)

period.as_reported: Market range compiled February 2025; literature search April 2025

study.method: No chemical analysis; arithmetic means of other studies' reported means

unresolved: All concentrations in the paper (e.g. fish-based puree As about 0.2735 mg/kg and Hg 0.0084 mg/kg as averages of other studies) are quotes or averages of other publications; not recorded as findings. Table S1 (supplement) not filed.

Labelling survey: fish-based purees were 12.04-13.13% of pureed baby food supply, fish content about 8%, hake about 50% of fish-based products, rice in 65%, carrots in 70%, potatoes in 80% (Figure 2); not metal measurements.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU maximum level for inorganic arsenic in foods for infants and young children, Regulation (EU) 2023/915, as quoted
Limits for baby foods quoted by the authors (source [34])
regulatory_or_exposure.value: Cd 0.040 mg/kg; Pb 0.020 mg/kg; Ni 0.50 mg/kg
